title: Visualisation of Bluetongue Virus in Culicoides Biting Midges
author: Guimerà Busquets, Brown, et al.

Total RNA was extracted from 100 µl of each insect homogenate using the KingFisher Flex robotic extraction system (ThermoFisher Scientific, Loughborough, UK) using the MagMAX™ CORE Nucleic Acid purification kit (ThermoFisher Scientific, Loughborough, UK) kit as per manufacturer’s instructions. Six microlitres of each extracted RNA was tested by qRT-PCR targeting Segment 10 (Seg-10) of BTV as described by [15], but adapted for the SuperScript III platinum one-step qRT-PCR (Invitrogen™, Life Technologies, Inchinnan, UK). Viral genome copies were quantified using a 10-fold dilution series of BTV-1 Seg-10 RNA transcript as standard [33]. qRT-PCR results were plotted using GraphPad Prism software version 9.3.1 (GraphPad Software, San Diego, USA).

steps.title: Infect female Culicoides
steps.instruction: Expose female C. sonorensis (PIRB‑s‑3) or C. nubeculosus (PIRB) to Bluetongue virus by either membrane feeding on horse blood containing 7.4 log10 TCID50 mL⁻¹ BTV‑4 MOR2009/07 or intrathoracic inoculation with ≤0.2 µL of virus at 6.4 log10 TCID50 mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Incubate infected insects
steps.instruction: Maintain the infected females at the appropriate temperature for 5–15 days (duration chosen per experiment).

steps.title: Anesthetize and dissect salivary apparatus
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the incubated insects with CO₂, then dissect heads while keeping the salivary apparatus (salivary glands and accessory glands) attached to the head; collect any additional soft organs of interest.

steps.title: Fix and permeabilise tissue
steps.instruction: Fix the dissected salivary apparatus in 4 % paraformaldehyde, then permeabilise in 0.5 % Triton X‑100 in PBS.

steps.title: Immunolabel tubulin, viral proteins and nuclei
steps.instruction: Incubate the permeabilised tissue with primary antibodies: mouse anti‑tubulin (Sigma‑Aldrich), guinea‑pig anti‑BTV structural proteins (Orab279, in‑house), and rabbit anti‑NS2 (Orab1, in‑house). Follow with appropriate secondary antibodies: anti‑mouse IgG AlexaFluor 405 or 568, anti‑guinea‑pig IgG AlexaFluor 488, and anti‑rabbit IgG AlexaFluor 568 (all Invitrogen). Counter‑stain nuclei with DAPI (Life Technologies).

steps.title: Mount labelled salivary apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the labelled salivary apparatus (head still attached) on a microscope slide inside a 25 µL gene‑frame (10 mm × 10 mm; Thermo Scientific) and add Vectashield® Hardset Mounting Medium (Vector Laboratories).

steps.title: Image with confocal microscope
steps.instruction: Acquire confocal images using a Leica SP8 CLSM (Leica Microsystems) and process the data with Leica Application Suite X.

steps.title: Homogenise matched bodies and salivary apparatus
steps.instruction: Pair each dissected salivary apparatus with its corresponding body, then homogenise the combined sample in a Tissue Lyzer (Qiagen).

steps.title: Extract viral RNA
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA from 100 µL of each homogenate using the MagMAX™ CORE Nucleic Acid purification kit on a KingFisher Flex robot (ThermoFisher Scientific) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Detect and quantify BTV RNA by RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Use 6 µL of the extracted RNA in a one‑step RT‑qPCR targeting BTV Segment 10, employing SuperScript III Platinum One‑Step qRT‑PCR reagents (Invitrogen) and the assay adapted from reference [15]. Quantify genome copies with a 10‑fold dilution series of a BTV‑1 Segment‑10 RNA transcript standard. Plot results in GraphPad Prism v9.3.1.
